counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest opposing consideration: the 100 sites lie sequentially along a single 350 km coastline, so spatial autocorrelation between neighbouring sites could in principle weaken the independence assumed by the chi-square test. However, this is a spatial-dependence concern, not repeated entry of the same authorized unit, and the description asserts sites are at least 3.5 km apart and are separate units; it therefore does not demonstrate the target issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: sites spaced every 3.5 km along one contiguous coast

source_refs.quoted_text:
Field crews walked a 350 km stretch of open coast and stopped at a fixed marker every
3.5 km, which gave 100 restoration sites separated by at least 3.5 km of shoreline.

counterevidence_considered.description: The reported p-value (0.049787) sits just below alpha = 0.05, so the rejection decision is fragile; but the value is arithmetically correct for the observed counts and its marginality is not evidence of any unit entering the procedure more than once.

source_refs.quoted_text:

- Effect size (Cohen's w): 0.2449

evidence.description: The data description states each independent unit (site_id) appears exactly once and that there are no repeat visits, subplots, or sub-samples, so the 100 rows are 100 separate sites.

There are no repeat visits, no subplots and no sub-samples anywhere in the file. Nothing
is nested inside anything else: the survey recorded one line per site, so the 100 lines

evidence.description: The input CSV contains exactly 100 data rows with unique site identifiers FD-001 through FD-100 (header on line 1; first and last data rows shown). No site_id repeats.
The workflow enforces uniqueness of the independent unit: read_sites raises a ValueError if any site_id appears more than once, so a repeated-unit entry cannot silently reach the test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate site_id guard present in read_sites

source_refs.quoted_text: """Return the survey rows, checking that every site appears exactly once."""

evidence.description: The tally and test consume each row exactly once with no resampling, joining, or expansion: tally_classes runs a single Counter pass over the rows, and stats.chisquare is applied to those per-site counts. The reported n of 100 equals the number of unique sites, and the counts 48+39+13 sum to 100.
evidence.observed_value: n = 100; counts 48 sparse / 39 patchy / 13 closed; chi-square(2) = 6.0000, p = 0.049787 (arithmetic independently verified: 2.4 + 2.7 + 0.9 = 6.0)

source_refs.quoted_text: - Independent units: 100 restoration sites, one row per site (site identifiers verified unique).

[selected-result] Chi-square goodness-of-fit on 100 independent restoration sites (one classification per site): chi-square(2) = 6.0000, p = 0.049787, Cohen's w = 0.2449; the 2024 cover-class composition (48 sparse / 39 patchy / 13 closed) differs from the 2019 reference composition of 0.60 / 0.30 / 0.10 at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I actively searched for any way an independent unit (site_id) could enter the chi-square procedure more than once: (1) scanned all 100 data rows of data/input.csv for duplicate site_id values — FD-001 through FD-100 each appear exactly once; (2) traced the workflow end to end for row duplication mechanisms (merges, appends, resampling, bootstrapping, per-subunit expansion) — read_sites performs one pass with an explicit duplicate-site_id guard that raises ValueError, and tally_classes does a single Counter pass, so each row contributes exactly one count; (3) cross-checked the reported n = 100 against the number of unique sites and recomputed the statistic (contributions 144/60 + 81/30 + 9/10 = 6.0, df = 2, p = exp(-3) ≈ 0.049787, w = sqrt(6/100) ≈ 0.2449), which matches the report exactly, confirming no inflated count reached the test. All attempts to demonstrate repeated-unit entry failed.
